title: Blood Magic
summary: The many kinds of sorcery Kindred work through vitae.

claims.text: Thaumaturgy is the most common vampiric magic, but it was not the first kind of blood magic and is still not the only one.
Thaumaturges hoard records, and most of them prove either unusable or unreliable.
A Kindred takes drunk blood straight into the body and can use it to fuel a ritual; a mortal who drinks blood only digests it, and its power is lost.

title: Ancient Blood Magicians
summary: Blood magic in the earliest Kindred societies.

claims.text: When the Second City fell, survivors blamed the blood magicians, whose costly and secretive work made them easy targets.
Ugaritic records tell of blood magicians who tried to remake mortal society with spirit bindings and failed badly.
Many demons that Jewish and later Christian holy men drove out in Palestine gathered around the hidden graves of Middle Eastern blood magicians.

title: Why the Tremere Study Thaumaturgy
summary: Ambition and survival behind Tremere research.

claims.text: Kindred magi still spend great time and wealth on old texts and new sorceries, though the Discipline is young by Kindred reckoning.
Ambition and the need to survive drove Clan Tremere to master blood magic from its first nights.

title: Thaumaturgic Curses
summary: A path for laying curses, sought by younger Kindred against elders.

claims.text: Young Kindred facing Gehenna pursue a path that turns the weaknesses of the Embrace against their elders, which feeds elder paranoia.
Its weakest curse marks the victim with an unseen stigma: people avoid the victim and find the victim hard to take seriously, until the next sunset.
A victim can throw off a curse by force of will, and the caster can lift a curse at any time, which makes it a bargaining chip.

title: Other Kindred Sorceries
summary: Assamite, Setite and koldunic sorcery as separate from Thaumaturgy.

claims.text: Assamite viziers learn Assamite sorcery, Setites their own magic and Tzimisce koldun koldunic sorcery, replacing the rough Thaumaturgy given to those clans in the core rules.
These sorceries cost the same experience to raise as Thaumaturgy.
Necromancers hold that the deep revulsion around corpses and remains is what makes their magic work.
A second principle, Authority, arose in the third century and drew on the theurgy of Iamblichus, which ranked gods, heroes, ghosts, angels and demons in one order a magician could command.

title: Gargoyles
summary: Winged Kindred made by Tremere sorcery.

claims.text: Gargoyles are Kindred created by sorcery and Old World vampire blood, built like the stone guardians of medieval buildings and able to fly.
The ritual is Level Five. It takes a large amount of vitae from two donors, each a Gangrel, Nosferatu or Tzimisce, plus a mortal who is transformed.
The Tremere use such creatures sparingly or in secret, since too many would draw notice.
